o: «En Florencia, ciudad rica y famosa de Italia, en la provincia que llaman Toscana, vivían Anselmo y Lotario, dos caballeros ricos y principales, y tan amigos que, por excelencia y antonomasia, de todos los que los conocían los dos amigos eran llamados.
t: "In Florence, the rich and famous city of Italy, in the province they call Tuscany, there lived Anselmo and Lotario, two rich and noble knights, and such friends that, by excellence and antonomasia, of all who knew them the two friends were called."

o: Eran solteros, mozos de una misma edad y de unas mismas costumbres; todo lo cual era bastante causa a que los dos con recíproca amistad se correspondiesen.
t: They were bachelors, young men of one and the same age and of one and the same habits; all which was reason enough for the two to correspond with each other in mutual friendship.

o: Pero, ¿dónde se hallará amigo tan discreto y tan leal y verdadero como aquí Lotario le pide?
t: But where shall a friend be found so discreet, so loyal and so true as he whom Lotario here asks for?

o: Así que, en quejas del uno y disculpas del otro se pasaban muchos ratos y partes del día.
t: So, in the complaints of the one and the excuses of the other they spent many hours and parts of the day.

o: »—Así es la verdad —respondió Anselmo—, y con esa confianza te hago saber, amigo Lotario, que el deseo que me fatiga es pensar si Camila, mi esposa, es tan buena y tan perfeta como yo pienso; y no puedo enterarme en esta verdad, si no es probándola de manera que la prueba manifieste los quilates de su bondad, como el fuego muestra los del oro.
t: "That is the truth," answered Anselmo, "and with that confidence I tell you, friend Lotario, that the desire which troubles me is to think whether Camila, my wife, is as good and as perfect as I believe; and I cannot learn this truth except by testing her in such a way that the test may reveal the fine gold of her goodness, as fire reveals the gold of metal."

o: Porque yo tengo para mí, ¡oh amigo!, que no es una mujer más buena de cuanto es o no es solicitada, y que aquella sola es fuerte que no se dobla a las promesas, a las dádivas, a las lágrimas y a las continuas importunidades de los solícitos amantes.
t: For I hold it, oh friend, that a woman is no better than she is or is not importuned, and that she alone is strong who does not yield to promises, to gifts, to tears, and to the constant importunities of eager lovers.

o: Porque, ¿qué hay que agradecer —decía él— que una mujer sea buena, si nadie le dice que sea mala?
t: For what is there to be thankful for," said he, "in a woman being good, if no one tells her that she is bad?"

o: ¿Qué mucho que esté recogida y temerosa la que no le dan ocasión para que se suelte, y la que sabe que tiene marido que, en cogiéndola en la primera desenvoltura, la ha de quitar la vida?
t: How much is it to be reserved and timid if she is given no occasion to let herself go, and if she knows she has a husband who, catching her in the first indiscretion, will take her life?

o: Ansí que, la que es buena por temor, o por falta de lugar, yo no la quiero tener en aquella estima en que tendré a la solicitada y perseguida que salió con la corona del vencimiento.
t: So, she who is good from fear, or for want of opportunity, I do not wish to hold in that esteem in which I shall hold the wooed and pursued one who came out with the crown of victory.

o: Y, cuando esto suceda al revés de lo que pienso, con el gusto de ver que acerté en mi opinión, llevaré sin pena la que de razón podrá causarme mi tan costosa experiencia.
t: And should this happen the reverse of what I think, with the satisfaction of seeing that I was right in my opinion, I shall bear without regret the loss of her who, in right and reason, may cost me so dearly through my experience.

o: Así que, si quieres que yo tenga vida que pueda decir que lo es, desde luego has de entrar en esta amorosa batalla, no tibia ni perezosamente, sino con el ahínco y diligencia que mi deseo pide, y con la confianza que nuestra amistad me asegura.
t: So, if you want me to have a life that I can call such, you must straightway enter into this amorous battle, neither lukewarm nor lazily, but with the zeal and diligence my desire demands, and with the confidence our friendship assures me.

o: Sin duda imagino, o que no me conoces, o que yo no te conozco.
t: Without doubt I imagine either that you do not know me, or that I do not know you.

o: Pues, si esto sintió un gentil de la amistad, ¿cuánto mejor es que lo sienta el cristiano, que sabe que por ninguna humana ha de perder la amistad divina?
t: Now, if a gentleman of friendship felt this, how much better is it that a Christian feel it, who knows that for no human thing must he lose divine friendship?

o: Y cuando el amigo tirase tanto la barra que pusiese aparte los respetos del cielo por acudir a los de su amigo, no ha de ser por cosas ligeras y de poco momento, sino por aquellas en que vaya la honra y la vida de su amigo.
t: And should the friend pull the bar so hard that he set aside the respects of heaven to attend to those of his friend, it must not be for light and trivial matters, but for those in which his friend's honour and life are at stake.

o: Pues dime tú ahora, Anselmo: ¿cuál destas dos cosas tienes en peligro para que yo me aventure a complacerte y a hacer una cosa tan detestable como me pides?
t: So tell me now, Anselmo: which of these two things have you in danger, that I should venture to please you and do a thing so detestable as you ask of me?

o: Ninguna, por cierto; antes, me pides, según yo entiendo, que procure y solicite quitarte la honra y la vida, y quitármela a mí juntamente.
t: None, indeed; rather, as I understand, you ask me to seek and strive to take away your honour and your life, and mine along with yours.

o: Porque si yo he de procurar quitarte la honra, claro está que te quito la vida, pues el hombre sin honra peor es que un muerto; y, siendo yo el instrumento, como tú quieres que lo sea, de tanto mal tuyo, ¿no vengo a quedar deshonrado, y, por el mesmo consiguiente, sin vida?
t: For if I am to seek to take away your honour, it is clear that I take your life as well, since a man without honour is worse than a dead man; and, being the instrument, as you wish me to be, of so much harm to you, do I not come away dishonoured and, consequently, without life?

o: Escucha, amigo Anselmo, y ten paciencia de no responderme hasta que acabe de decirte lo que se me ofreciere acerca de lo que te ha pedido tu deseo; que tiempo quedará para que tú me repliques y yo te escuche.
t: Listen, friend Anselmo, and have patience not to answer me until I finish telling you what occurs to me about what your desire has asked of you; there will be time enough for you to reply and for me to listen.

o: »—Que me place —dijo Anselmo—: di lo que quisieres.
t: "It pleases me," said Anselmo; "say whatever you like."

o: »Y Lotario prosiguió diciendo.
t: And Lotario went on to say.

o: Y, porque claro lo veas, dime, Anselmo: ¿tú no me has dicho que tengo de solicitar a una retirada, persuadir a una honesta, ofrecer a una desinteresada, servir a una prudente?
t: And so that you may clearly see it, tell me, Anselmo: have I not told you that you must seek out a secluded woman, persuade an honest one, offer yourself to a disinterested one, and serve a prudent one?

o: Sí que me lo has dicho.
t: Yes, you have told me that.

o: Pues si tú sabes que tienes mujer retirada, honesta, desinteresada y prudente, ¿qué buscas?
t: Well then, if you know that you have a woman secluded, honest, disinterested and prudent, what are you after?

o: Y si piensas que de todos mis asaltos ha de salir vencedora, como saldrá sin duda, ¿qué mejores títulos piensas darle después que los que ahora tiene, o qué será más después de lo que es ahora?
t: And if you think that from all my assaults she must come off victorious, as she undoubtedly will, what better titles do you think to give her afterward than those she has now, or what will she be afterward that she is not now?

o: O es que tú no la tienes por la que dices, o tú no sabes lo que pides.
t: Either you do not hold her to be what you say, or you do not know what you are asking for.

o: Si no la tienes por lo que dices, ¿para qué quieres probarla, sino, como a mala, hacer della lo que más te viniere en gusto?
t: If you do not hold her to be what you say, why do you want to put her to the test, rather than, like a bad woman, make of her whatever best suits your whim?

o: Mas si es tan buena como crees, impertinente cosa será hacer experiencia de la mesma verdad, pues, después de hecha, se ha de quedar con la estimación que primero tenía.
t: But if she is as good as you believe, it would be an impertinent thing to make trial of her in truth, for once the trial is made she must remain with the esteem she first had.

o: Así que, es razón concluyente que el intentar las cosas de las cuales antes nos puede suceder daño que provecho es de juicios sin discurso y temerarios, y más cuando quieren intentar aquellas a que no son forzados ni compelidos, y que de muy lejos traen descubierto que el intentarlas es manifiesta locura.
t: So it is a conclusive reason that attempting things from which harm rather than good can come to us is the work of thoughtless and reckless judgments, and still more so when they want to attempt those things to which they are neither forced nor compelled, and which they see from far off that attempting them is sheer folly.

o: Estas cosas son las que suelen intentarse, y es honra, gloria y provecho intentarlas, aunque tan llenas de inconvenientes y peligros.
t: These are the things that are usually attempted, and it is honor, glory and profit to attempt them, however full of difficulties and dangers they may be.

o: Y, para confirmación desta verdad, te quiero decir una estancia que hizo el famoso poeta Luis Tansilo, en el fin de su primera parte de Las lágrimas de San Pedro, que dice así.
t: And, in confirmation of this truth, I want to tell you a stanza that the famous poet Luis Tansilo wrote at the end of the first part of *The Tears of Saint Peter*, which says this.

o: Crece el dolor y crece la vergüenza en Pedro, cuando el día se ha mostrado; y, aunque allí no ve a nadie, se avergüenza de sí mesmo, por ver que había pecado: que a un magnánimo pecho a haber vergüenza no sólo ha de moverle el ser mirado; que de sí se avergüenza cuando yerra, si bien otro no vee que cielo y tierra.
t: In Peter both pain and shame grow greater, when the day has shown itself; and though there he sees no one, he is ashamed of himself, on seeing that there was sin: for in a magnanimous breast, shame at having sinned must not only be moved by being seen by others; he is ashamed of himself when he errs, though no one but heaven and earth sees it.

o: Cuanto más que, con lo que ahora pienso decirte, acabarás de venir en conocimiento del grande error que quieres cometer.
t: Moreover, with what I now mean to tell you, you will come to know the great error you wish to commit.

o: Y más, si lo pusieses por obra; que, puesto caso que la piedra hiciese resistencia a tan necia prueba, no por eso se le añadiría más valor ni más fama; y si se rompiese, cosa que podría ser, ¿no se perdería todo?
t: And more: if you were to put it into practice, granting that the stone offered resistance to so foolish a test, it would not thereby gain more worth or more fame; and if it broke, which is possible, would not everything be lost?

o: Sí, por cierto, dejando a su dueño en estimación de que todos le tengan por simple.
t: Yes, certainly, leaving its owner with the reputation of being held a fool by everyone.

o: Mira que no hay joya en el mundo que tanto valga como la mujer casta y honrada, y que todo el honor de las mujeres consiste en la opinión buena que dellas se tiene; y, pues la de tu esposa es tal que llega al estremo de bondad que sabes, ¿para qué quieres poner esta verdad en duda?
t: Consider that there is no jewel in the world worth as much as a chaste and honorable woman, and that all the honor of women consists in the good opinion held of them; and since your wife's is such as reaches the extreme of goodness that you know, why do you want to put this truth in doubt?

o: Mira, amigo, que la mujer es animal imperfecto, y que no se le han de poner embarazos donde tropiece y caiga, sino quitárselos y despejalle el camino de cualquier inconveniente, para que sin pesadumbre corra ligera a alcanzar la perfeción que le falta, que consiste en el ser virtuosa.
t: Consider, friend, that woman is an imperfect animal, and that you must not set obstacles in her way where she may stumble and fall, but rather take them away and clear her path of every hindrance, so that she may run lightly and without heaviness to attain the perfection she lacks, which consists in being virtuous.

o: Es asimesmo la buena mujer como espejo de cristal luciente y claro; pero está sujeto a empañarse y escurecerse con cualquiera aliento que le toque.
t: Likewise, a good woman is like a shining, clear crystal mirror; but she is subject to being clouded and darkened by any breath that touches her.

o: Hase de usar con la honesta mujer el estilo que con las reliquias: adorarlas y no tocarlas.
t: One must use with an honest woman the same style one uses with relics: adore them and not touch them.

o: Hase de guardar y estimar la mujer buena como se guarda y estima un hermoso jardín que está lleno de flores y rosas, cuyo dueño no consiente que nadie le pasee ni manosee; basta que desde lejos, y por entre las verjas de hierro, gocen de su fragrancia y hermosura.
t: A good woman must be kept and cherished as one keeps and cherishes a beautiful garden full of flowers and roses, whose owner does not allow anyone to walk in it or handle it; it is enough that from afar, and through the iron bars, people enjoy its fragrance and beauty.

o: Finalmente, quiero decirte unos versos que se me han venido a la memoria, que los oí en una comedia moderna, que me parece que hacen al propósito de lo que vamos tratando.
t: Finally, I want to tell you some verses that came to mind, which I heard in a modern play, and which seem to me to fit the subject we have been discussing.

o: Aconsejaba un prudente viejo a otro, padre de una doncella, que la recogiese, guardase y encerrase, y entre otras razones, le dijo éstas.
t: A prudent old man advised another, the father of a young woman, that he should take her in, keep her safe, and shut her away, and among other reasons he gave him these.

o: Es de vidrio la mujer; pero no se ha de probar si se puede o no quebrar, porque todo podría ser.
t: A woman is made of glass; but one must not test whether it can be broken or not, because anything might happen.

o: Y es más fácil el quebrarse, y no es cordura ponerse a peligro de romperse lo que no puede soldarse.
t: And it is easier to break, and it is not wise to put at risk of breaking what cannot be soldered back together.

o: Y en esta opinión estén todos, y en razón la fundo: que si hay Dánaes en el mundo, hay pluvias de oro también.
t: And let everyone hold this opinion, and on this ground I base it: if there are Danaës in the world, there are also golden rains.

o: Cuanto hasta aquí te he dicho, ¡oh Anselmo!, ha sido por lo que a ti te toca; y ahora es bien que se oiga algo de lo que a mí me conviene; y si fuere largo, perdóname, que todo lo requiere el laberinto donde te has entrado y de donde quieres que yo te saque.
t: Everything I have told you so far, oh Anselmo, has been about what concerns you; and now it is good that something be heard of what concerns me; and if it be long, forgive me, for the labyrinth into which you have entered, and from which you want me to lead you out, requires it all.

o: Tú me tienes por amigo y quieres quitarme la honra, cosa que es contra toda amistad; y aun no sólo pretendes esto, sino que procuras que yo te la quite a ti.
t: You consider me a friend and you want to take away my honor, a thing contrary to all friendship; and not only do you aim at this, but you seek to make me take it away from you.

o: Que me la quieres quitar a mí está claro, pues, cuando Camila vea que yo la solicito, como me pides, cierto está que me ha de tener por hombre sin honra y mal mirado, pues intento y hago una cosa tan fuera de aquello que el ser quien soy y tu amistad me obliga.
t: That you want to take it from me is clear, for when Camila sees that I court her, as you ask me to, she will certainly hold me to be a man without honor and ill-regarded, since I intend and do a thing so far removed from what my being who I am and your friendship oblige me to.

o: De que quieres que te la quite a ti no hay duda, porque, viendo Camila que yo la solicito, ha de pensar que yo he visto en ella alguna liviandad que me dio atrevimiento a descubrirle mi mal deseo; y, teniéndose por deshonrada, te toca a ti, como a cosa suya, su mesma deshonra.
t: There is no doubt that you want me to take it from you, because, seeing Camila that I court her, she must think I have seen in her some lightness that gave me the boldness to disclose my bad desire; and, considering herself dishonored, her very dishonor falls to you, as her own concern.

o: Pero quiérote decir la causa por que con justa razón es deshonrado el marido de la mujer mala, aunque él no sepa que lo es, ni tenga culpa, ni haya sido parte, ni dado ocasión, para que ella lo sea.
t: But I meant to tell you the reason why the husband of a bad woman is justly dishonored, even though he does not know that she is bad, nor is at fault, nor has been a party to it, nor given occasion for her to be so.

o: Y no te canses de oírme, que todo ha de redundar en tu provecho.
t: And do not tire of hearing me out, for all of it must turn to your benefit.

o: Cuando Dios crió a nuestro primero padre en el Paraíso terrenal, dice la Divina Escritura que infundió Dios sueño en Adán, y que, estando durmiendo, le sacó una costilla del lado siniestro, de la cual formó a nuestra madre Eva; y, así como Adán despertó y la miró, dijo: ''Ésta es carne de mi carne y hueso de mis huesos''.
t: When God created our first father in the earthly Paradise, Holy Scripture says, God cast a sleep upon Adam, and, while he slept, took a rib from his left side, from which he formed our mother Eve; and, as Adam awoke and looked at her, he said: 'This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh.'

o: Y Dios dijo: ''Por ésta dejará el hombre a su padre y madre, y serán dos en una carne misma''.
t: And God said: 'Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be two in one flesh.'

o: Y entonces fue instituido el divino sacramento del matrimonio, con tales lazos que sola la muerte puede desatarlos.
t: And then the divine sacrament of marriage was instituted, with such bonds that only death can loose them.

o: Y tiene tanta fuerza y virtud este milagroso sacramento, que hace que dos diferentes personas sean una mesma carne; y aún hace más en los buenos casados, que, aunque tienen dos almas, no tienen más de una voluntad.
t: And this miraculous sacrament has so much force and power that it makes two different persons into one same flesh; and it does still more among the good married, who, though they have two souls, have no more than one will.

o: Y de aquí viene que, como la carne de la esposa sea una mesma con la del esposo, las manchas que en ella caen, o los defectos que se procura, redundan en la carne del marido, aunque él no haya dado, como queda dicho, ocasión para aquel daño.
t: And hence it comes that, since the flesh of the wife is one and the same with that of the husband, the stains that fall upon her, or the defects she is given to, redound upon the husband's flesh, even though, as has been said, he gave no occasion for that harm.

o: Porque, así como el dolor del pie o de cualquier miembro del cuerpo humano le siente todo el cuerpo, por ser todo de una carne mesma, y la cabeza siente el daño del tobillo, sin que ella se le haya causado, así el marido es participante de la deshonra de la mujer, por ser una mesma cosa con ella.
t: Because, just as the pain of the foot or of any member of the human body is felt by the whole body, since it is all one same flesh, and the head feels the hurt of the ankle, though it was not caused to it, so the husband shares in the dishonor of the woman, because he is one and the same thing with her.

o: Y como las honras y deshonras del mundo sean todas y nazcan de carne y sangre, y las de la mujer mala sean deste género, es forzoso que al marido le quepa parte dellas, y sea tenido por deshonrado sin que él lo sepa.
t: And since the honors and dishonors of the world are all of them, and are born of flesh and blood, and those of the bad woman are of this kind, it is inevitable that a share of them fall to the husband, and that he be held dishonored without knowing it.

o: Mira, pues, ¡oh Anselmo!, al peligro que te pones en querer turbar el sosiego en que tu buena esposa vive.
t: Look, Anselmo, my friend, at the risk you run in wanting to disturb the peace in which your good wife lives.

o: Mira por cuán vana e impertinente curiosidad quieres revolver los humores que ahora están sosegados en el pecho de tu casta esposa.
t: See how vain and impertinent a curiosity moves you to stir up the humors that are now settled in the breast of your chaste wife.

o: Advierte que lo que aventuras a ganar es poco, y que lo que perderás será tanto que lo dejaré en su punto, porque me faltan palabras para encarecerlo.
t: Understand that what you venture to gain is little, and what you will lose is so much that I will leave it unsaid, for I lack words to praise it.

o: Pero si todo cuanto he dicho no basta a moverte de tu mal propósito, bien puedes buscar otro instrumento de tu deshonra y desventura, que yo no pienso serlo, aunque por ello pierda tu amistad, que es la mayor pérdida que imaginar puedo.
t: But if all I have said is not enough to turn you from your bad purpose, you may go looking for another instrument of your dishonor and misfortune, for I have no mind to be one, even at the cost of losing your friendship, which is the greatest loss I can imagine.

o: »Calló, en diciendo esto, el virtuoso y prudente Lotario, y Anselmo quedó tan confuso y pensativo que por un buen espacio no le pudo responder palabra; pero, en fin, le dijo.
t: With that, the virtuous and prudent Lothario fell silent, and Anselmo was so confused and thoughtful that for a good while he could not answer him a word; but at last he said:

o: »—Con la atención que has visto he escuchado, Lotario amigo, cuanto has querido decirme, y en tus razones, ejemplos y comparaciones he visto la mucha discreción que tienes y el estremo de la verdadera amistad que alcanzas; y ansimesmo veo y confieso que si no sigo tu parecer y me voy tras el mío, voy huyendo del bien y corriendo tras el mal.
t: With the attention you have seen, dear Lothario, I have listened to everything you wished to tell me, and in your arguments, examples and comparisons I have seen the great discretion you possess and the height of true friendship you attain; and I likewise see and confess that if I do not follow your counsel and instead follow my own, I am fleeing from the good and running after the evil.

o: Y, pues tan poco aventuras y tanto contento me puedes dar aventurándote, no lo dejes de hacer, aunque más inconvenientes se te pongan delante, pues, como ya he dicho, con sólo que comiences daré por concluida la causa.
t: And since you can give me so little risk and so much happiness by venturing, do not fail to do it, even if more difficulties are placed in your way, for, as I have already said, once you begin I shall consider the matter settled.

o: Abrazóle Anselmo tierna y amorosamente, y agradecióle su ofrecimiento, como si alguna grande merced le hubiera hecho; y quedaron de acuerdo entre los dos que desde otro día siguiente se comenzase la obra; que él le daría lugar y tiempo como a sus solas pudiese hablar a Camila, y asimesmo le daría dineros y joyas que darla y que ofrecerla.
t: Anselmo embraced him tenderly and lovingly and thanked him for his offer, as though some great favor had been done him; and the two agreed that from the next day onward they would begin the work: that he would give him opportunity and time to speak with Camila as he pleased, and would likewise give him money and jewels to give her and to offer her.

o: Aconsejóle que le diese músicas, que escribiese versos en su alabanza, y que, cuando él no quisiese tomar trabajo de hacerlos, él mesmo los haría.
t: He advised him to have music played, to write verses in her praise, and that whenever he did not care to take the trouble of making them, he would make them himself.

o: A todo se ofreció Lotario, bien con diferente intención que Anselmo pensaba.
t: Lothario offered himself for everything, though with an intention different from what Anselmo supposed.

o: »Y con este acuerdo se volvieron a casa de Anselmo, donde hallaron a Camila con ansia y cuidado, esperando a su esposo, porque aquel día tardaba en venir más de lo acostumbrado.
t: With this agreement they returned to Anselmo's house, where they found Camila anxious and worried, waiting for her husband, because that day he was taking longer to come than usual.

o: »Fuese Lotario a su casa, y Anselmo quedó en la suya, tan contento como Lotario fue pensativo, no sabiendo qué traza dar para salir bien de aquel impertinente negocio.
t: Lothario went to his own house, and Anselmo stayed in his, as happy as Lothario was pensive, not knowing what scheme to devise to come out of that impertinent business well.

o: Rogóle Camila que no se fuese y Lotario se ofreció a hacerle compañía, más nada aprovechó con Anselmo; antes, importunó a Lotario que se quedase y le aguardase, porque tenía que tratar con él una cosa de mucha importancia.
t: Camila asked him not to go, and Lothario offered to keep her company; nothing availed with Anselmo; rather, he importuned Lothario to stay and wait for him, because he had to discuss with him a matter of great importance.

o: Dijo también a Camila que no dejase solo a Lotario en tanto que él volviese.
t: He also told Camila not to leave Lothario alone while he was away.

o: En efeto, él supo tan bien fingir la necesidad, o necedad, de su ausencia, que nadie pudiera entender que era fingida.
t: In effect, he knew so well how to pretend the need, or folly, of his absence, that no one could tell it was pretended.

o: Fuese Anselmo, y quedaron solos a la mesa Camila y Lotario, porque la demás gente de casa toda se había ido a comer.
t: Anselmo went, and Camila and Lothario were left alone at table, because all the rest of the household had gone off to eat.

o: Viose Lotario puesto en la estacada que su amigo deseaba y con el enemigo delante, que pudiera vencer con sola su hermosura a un escuadrón de caballeros armados: mirad si era razón que le temiera Lotario.
t: Lothario found himself set in the lists his friend desired, with the enemy before him, who could defeat a squadron of armed knights with his beauty alone: judge if Lothario had reason to fear him.

o: »Pero lo que hizo fue poner el codo sobre el brazo de la silla y la mano abierta en la mejilla, y, pidiendo perdón a Camila del mal comedimiento, dijo que quería reposar un poco en tanto que Anselmo volvía.
t: But what he did was rest his elbow on the arm of the chair and lay his open hand on his cheek, and, asking Camila's pardon for his bad manners, said that he wanted to rest a little while Anselmo returned.

o: Camila le respondió que mejor reposaría en el estrado que en la silla, y así, le rogó se entrase a dormir en él.
t: Camila told him he would rest better on the couch than in the chair, and so she asked him to go in and sleep on it.

o: Todo esto le contentó mucho a Anselmo, y dijo que cada día daría el mesmo lugar, aunque no saliese de casa, porque en ella se ocuparía en cosas que Camila no pudiese venir en conocimiento de su artificio.
t: All this delighted Anselmo greatly, and he said he would give him the same opportunity every day, even if he did not leave the house, because in it he would occupy himself with things Camila could not come to know of his cunning.

o: »Lotario respondió que ya que había comenzado, que él llevaría hasta el fin aquella empresa, puesto que entendía salir della cansado y vencido.
t: "Lotario replied that since he had begun, he would carry that enterprise through to the end, since he understood he would come out of it tired and vanquished.

o: Otro día recibió los cuatro mil escudos, y con ellos cuatro mil confusiones, porque no sabía qué decirse para mentir de nuevo; pero, en efeto, determinó de decirle que Camila estaba tan entera a las dádivas y promesas como a las palabras, y que no había para qué cansarse más, porque todo el tiempo se gastaba en balde.
t: Another day he received the four thousand escudos, and with them four thousand confusions, because he did not know what to say to himself in order to lie again; but in effect he determined to tell her that Camila was as untouched by gifts and promises as by words, and that there was no point in troubling himself further, since all his time was being wasted in vain.

o: Y, para ver si esto era ansí, salió del aposento, y, llamando a Lotario aparte, le preguntó qué nuevas había y de qué temple estaba Camila.
t: And, to see whether this were so, he left the room and, calling Lotario aside, asked him what news there was and what temper Camila was in.

o: Lotario le respondió que no pensaba más darle puntada en aquel negocio, porque respondía tan áspera y desabridamente, que no tendría ánimo para volver a decirle cosa alguna.
t: Lotario replied that he meant to have nothing more to do with that business, because she answered so harshly and so ungraciously that he would not have the heart to say anything to her again.

o: »—¡Ah! —dijo Anselmo—, Lotario, Lotario, y cuán mal correspondes a lo que me debes y a lo mucho que de ti confío!
t: "Ah!" said Anselmo, "Lotario, Lotario, and how ill you repay what I owe you and how much I trust in you!"

o: Ahora te he estado mirando por el lugar que concede la entrada desta llave, y he visto que no has dicho palabra a Camila, por donde me doy a entender que aun las primeras le tienes por decir; y si esto es así, como sin duda lo es, ¿para qué me engañas, o por qué quieres quitarme con tu industria los medios que yo podría hallar para conseguir mi deseo?
t: I have been watching you from the place that overlooks the entrance of this keyhole, and I have seen that you have not said a word to Camila, from which I infer that you still have your first words to tell her; and if this is so, as it undoubtedly is, why do you deceive me, or why do you want to take from me by your cunning the means I might find to achieve my desire?

o: Creyóle Anselmo, y para dalle comodidad más segura y menos sobresaltada, determinó de hacer ausencia de su casa por ocho días, yéndose a la de un amigo suyo, que estaba en una aldea, no lejos de la ciudad, con el cual amigo concertó que le enviase a llamar con muchas veras, para tener ocasión con Camila de su partida.
t: Anselmo believed him, and in order to give her safer and less startling comfort, he determined to be absent from his house for eight days, going to the house of a friend of his who was in a village not far from the city, and with this friend he arranged that he would send to call him with great insistence, so as to have occasion to leave with Camila.

o: »¡Desdichado y mal advertido de ti, Anselmo!
t: "Unhappy and ill-advised of you, Anselmo!

o: ¿Qué es lo que haces?
t: What are you doing?

o: ¿Qué es lo que trazas?
t: What are you plotting?

o: ¿Qué es lo que ordenas?
t: What are you ordering?

o: Mira que haces contra ti mismo, trazando tu deshonra y ordenando tu perdición.
t: See how you work against yourself, plotting your dishonor and ordering your perdition.

o: Buena es tu esposa Camila, quieta y sosegadamente la posees, nadie sobresalta tu gusto, sus pensamientos no salen de las paredes de su casa, tú eres su cielo en la tierra, el blanco de sus deseos, el cumplimiento de sus gustos y la medida por donde mide su voluntad, ajustándola en todo con la tuya y con la del cielo.
t: Good is your wife Camila; you possess her quietly and peacefully, and no one disturbs your pleasure; her thoughts do not go beyond the walls of her house; you are her heaven on earth, the goal of her desires, the fulfillment of her wishes, and the measure by which she measures her will, adjusting it in everything to yours and to heaven's.

o: Pues si la mina de su honor, hermosura, honestidad y recogimiento te da sin ningún trabajo toda la riqueza que tiene y tú puedes desear, ¿para qué quieres ahondar la tierra y buscar nuevas vetas de nuevo y nunca visto tesoro, poniéndote a peligro que toda venga abajo, pues, en fin, se sustenta sobre los débiles arrimos de su flaca naturaleza?
t: Now if the mine of her honor, beauty, honesty and modesty yields you, without any labor, all the wealth it has and you could desire, why do you want to dig deeper into the earth and seek new veins of never-before-seen treasure, putting yourself in danger of everything collapsing, since, after all, it rests on the weak supports of her frail nature?

o: Mira que el que busca lo imposible es justo que lo posible se le niegue, como lo dijo mejor un poeta, diciendo.
t: See how it is just that he who seeks the impossible should be denied the possible, as a poet put it better, saying:

o: Busco en la muerte la vida, salud en la enfermedad, en la prisión libertad, en lo cerrado salida y en el traidor lealtad.
t: I seek life in death, health in sickness, freedom in prison, a way out in what is closed, and loyalty in the traitor.

o: Pero mi suerte, de quien jamás espero algún bien, con el cielo ha estatuido que, pues lo imposible pido, lo posible aun no me den.
t: But my fate, from whom I never hope for any good, has decreed with heaven that, since I ask for the impossible, the possible be not yet granted me.

o: »Fuese otro día Anselmo a la aldea, dejando dicho a Camila que el tiempo que él estuviese ausente vendría Lotario a mirar por su casa y a comer con ella; que tuviese cuidado de tratalle como a su mesma persona.
t: Anselmo went another day to the village, having told Camila that while he was away Lotario would come to look after his house and to dine with her; that she should take care to treat him as she would her own person.

o: Afligióse Camila, como mujer discreta y honrada, de la orden que su marido le dejaba, y díjole que advirtiese que no estaba bien que nadie, él ausente, ocupase la silla de su mesa, y que si lo hacía por no tener confianza que ella sabría gobernar su casa, que probase por aquella vez, y vería por experiencia como para mayores cuidados era bastante.
t: Camila was distressed, as a discreet and honorable woman, by the order her husband left her, and she told him to consider that it was not fitting that anyone, in his absence, should take the seat at her table, and that if he did so because he had no trust in her, she would know how to govern her house; let him try it that once, and he would see by experience that greater cares were unnecessary.

o: Anselmo le replicó que aquél era su gusto, y que no tenía más que hacer que bajar la cabeza y obedecelle.
t: Anselmo replied that that was his wish, and that he had nothing to do but bow his head and obey her.

o: »En los tres días primeros nunca Lotario le dijo nada, aunque pudiera, cuando se levantaban los manteles y la gente se iba a comer con mucha priesa, porque así se lo tenía mandado Camila.
t: "For the first three days Lotario never said a word to her, even when he might have, when the tablecloths were lifted and the company went off to eat in great haste, because Camila had so ordered it.

o: Y aun tenía orden Leonela que comiese primero que Camila, y que de su lado jamás se quitase; mas ella, que en otras cosas de su gusto tenía puesto el pensamiento y había menester aquellas horas y aquel lugar para ocuparle en sus contentos, no cumplía todas veces el mandamiento de su señora; antes, los dejaba solos, como si aquello le hubieran mandado.
t: Leonela also had orders to eat before Camila and never to leave her side; but she, who in other matters of her own taste had set her mind and needed those hours and that place to occupy herself with her pleasures, did not always carry out her mistress's command; instead, she left the two of them alone, as if she had been told to.

o: Mas la honesta presencia de Camila, la gravedad de su rostro, la compostura de su persona era tanta, que ponía freno a la lengua de Lotario.
t: But Camila's honest presence, the gravity of her face, the composure of her person was such that it put a rein on Lotario's tongue.

o: Hacíase fuerza y peleaba consigo mismo por desechar y no sentir el contento que le llevaba a mirar a Camila.
t: He forced himself and struggled with himself to cast off and not feel the delight that led him to look at Camila.

o: Culpábase a solas de su desatino, llamábase mal amigo y aun mal cristiano; hacía discursos y comparaciones entre él y Anselmo, y todos paraban en decir que más había sido la locura y confianza de Anselmo que su poca fidelidad, y que si así tuviera disculpa para con Dios como para con los hombres de lo que pensaba hacer, que no temiera pena por su culpa.
t: He blamed himself in private for his blunder, called himself a bad friend and even a bad Christian; he made speeches and comparisons between himself and Anselmo, and they all came down to saying that Anselmo's madness and trust had been more to blame than his own lack of fidelity, and that if he had as good an excuse before God as before men for what he meant to do, he would fear no punishment for his fault.

o: »En efecto, la hermosura y la bondad de Camila, juntamente con la ocasión que el ignorante marido le había puesto en las manos, dieron con la lealtad de Lotario en tierra.
t: "Indeed, Camila's beauty and goodness, together with the occasion the ignorant husband had placed in his hands, brought Lotario's loyalty to the ground.

o: Mas no por esta sequedad se desmayó en Lotario la esperanza, que siempre nace juntamente con el amor; antes, tuvo en más a Camila.
t: Yet Lotario's hope did not grow faint from this coldness, for hope is always born together with love; rather, he thought more highly of Camila than before.

o: La cual, habiendo visto en Lotario lo que jamás pensara, no sabía qué hacerse.
t: She, having seen in Lotario what she had never imagined, did not know what to do.

o: Y, pareciéndole no ser cosa segura ni bien hecha darle ocasión ni lugar a que otra vez la hablase, determinó de enviar aquella mesma noche, como lo hizo, a un criado suyo con un billete a Anselmo, donde le escribió estas razones.
t: And, thinking it neither safe nor well done to give him occasion or leave to speak to her again, she resolved to send that very night, as she did, one of her servants with a letter to Anselmo, in which she wrote these words.
